//: Single source of truth for which font file backs each FontFamily role (Title/SansSerif/Monospace — see FontFamily in src/compositor/types.rs). Rust's src/fonts.rs (via build.rs codegen) and web/'s TS/CSS all read this file instead of keeping their own copy of a filename or family-name literal. To experiment with a different Chinese font for a role, edit that role's entry below and drop the new font file into this fonts/ directory — no other file needs to change.
//sansSerif+monospace: `name` is the fontdb generic-alias target used by set_sans_serif_family/set_monospace_family in src/pdf.rs, and in principle can be any string as long as it agrees with the matching familyCss below. In practice though, familyCss's bare name is embedded as the *literal* first choice in the SVG's font-family list (e.g. '"Foo", sans-serif'), and fontdb resolves a literal name by matching a loaded font's own name-table family before it ever falls back to the sans-serif/monospace generic alias — so if the bare name doesn't match the actual font file's internal name-table family, PDF export silently drops that text's font (no embed, no error) instead of falling through to the alias. So in practice this MUST equal the font file's internal name-table family too, same as title below — check it with e.g. `fc-scan --format '%{family}\n' <file>` or fonttools before picking a value.
//title: Title has no `name` field: it's addressed by its own literal name-table family instead of a fontdb generic alias (fontdb resolves a literal font-family by matching a loaded font's own name-table family). So title's familyCss bare name *must* equal the actual font file's internal name-table family — swapping in a different font file for this role means updating that name to match the new file's own family, not an arbitrary choice like the other two roles.
